layouts.name: Deconstructed / Broken Grid
layouts.blurb: Elements deliberately ignore the columns — offset, overlapping, tilted.
layouts.rareBecause: It fights every grid instinct designers are trained on; feels 'wrong' until it's tuned.
layouts.reachFor: Fashion, art, portfolio, editorial brands that want to signal they don't follow rules.
layouts.watchOut: One misjudged offset reads as a bug, not a choice. Needs obsessive spacing control.

layouts.name: Diagonal / Skewed Sections
layouts.blurb: Section dividers cut across on an angle instead of flat horizontal lines.
layouts.rareBecause: Skew math breaks text alignment; most templates only ship straight bands.
layouts.reachFor: Tech, sports, energy brands wanting momentum and motion baked into the structure.
layouts.watchOut: Skewing the whole section skews the type too — you must counter-rotate content.

layouts.name: Overlapping Layers / Depth Collage
layouts.blurb: Cards and images sit on top of each other with real z-depth and shadow.
layouts.rareBecause: Overlap breaks predictable stacking and reflow — scary on responsive.
layouts.reachFor: Storytelling, case studies, 'scrapbook' brand worlds, culture-forward sites.
layouts.watchOut: Overlaps that work on desktop collapse into a pile on mobile without a reflow plan.

layouts.name: Extreme Asymmetry (80/20)
layouts.blurb: A radically off-center split — one side dominates, the other is a sliver.
layouts.rareBecause: Everyone defaults to 50/50 or 60/40; true 80/20 feels unbalanced at first.
layouts.reachFor: Bold statement heroes, single-product launches, photography-led brands.
layouts.watchOut: The sliver side gets ignored — only put low-priority or purely decorative content there.

layouts.name: Mondrian / Irregular Bento Mosaic
layouts.blurb: Uneven color-blocked cells of clashing sizes — asymmetric, painterly.
layouts.rareBecause: Standard bento is tidy and equal; a true Mondrian is deliberately unequal and loud.
layouts.reachFor: Brand landing pages, 'systems' products, anything that wants to feel composed yet alive.
layouts.watchOut: Without a strict color ratio it turns into visual noise. Limit to 3 accent fills.

layouts.name: Bento Breakout (cell escapes bounds)
layouts.blurb: One tile bursts past the grid edge, breaking the container it lives in.
layouts.rareBecause: It intentionally violates the box model everyone protects — overflow feels dangerous.
layouts.reachFor: Feature reveals, product hero moments, a single 'wow' beat on an otherwise clean page.
layouts.watchOut: Breakouts clipped by overflow:hidden vanish. Needs deliberate stacking + spacing room.
layouts.wireframe: BREAKOUT

layouts.name: Exposed Blueprint Grid
layouts.blurb: The construction grid is visible — ruled lines, coordinates, corner ticks.
layouts.rareBecause: Designers hide the grid; showing it reads as unfinished unless fully committed.
layouts.reachFor: Technical products, dev tools, architecture/engineering brands, data platforms.
layouts.watchOut: Half-committing looks like leftover dev guides. Go all-in or not at all.

layouts.name: Negative-Space Dominant
layouts.blurb: One tiny element adrift in a vast empty field. Silence as the design.
layouts.rareBecause: It feels 'empty' and unfinished to clients who equate value with density.
layouts.reachFor: Luxury, fine art, high-end studios, meditation/wellness — brands selling restraint.
layouts.watchOut: Requires flawless type and one perfect focal point. Nowhere for weak craft to hide.

layouts.name: Horizontal-Scroll Site
layouts.blurb: The whole page moves sideways instead of down.
layouts.rareBecause: It breaks the most basic web instinct — vertical scroll — and confuses first-time users.
layouts.reachFor: Portfolios, galleries, timelines, product tours where the story is inherently linear.
layouts.watchOut: Kills native scroll feel, hurts accessibility & SEO. Always give a vertical fallback.

layouts.name: Sticky Card Deck (scroll-stack)
layouts.blurb: Cards stack and pin on top of each other as you scroll, like dealing a hand.
layouts.rareBecause: The pinned-stacking scroll trick is fiddly and easy to make janky.
layouts.reachFor: Feature sequences, step stories, pricing reveals — anything that benefits from pacing.
layouts.watchOut: Overdone it feels gimmicky; too many cards and users lose the thread.

layouts.name: Scrollytelling (pinned narrative)
layouts.blurb: A visual pins on one side while text-driven steps scroll and update it.
layouts.rareBecause: Requires scroll-linked state; most builders can't do it without heavy JS.
layouts.reachFor: Data stories, product explainers, editorial features, cause/mission sites.
layouts.watchOut: Expensive to build & maintain; breaks badly if the scroll math drifts.
layouts.wireframe: PINNED

layouts.name: Split-Screen Dual Scroll
layouts.blurb: Two vertical halves scroll independently in opposite directions.
layouts.rareBecause: Two scroll contexts on one screen fights muscle memory and touch gestures.
layouts.reachFor: Comparison sites, dual-audience landing (e.g. buyers vs sellers), lookbooks.
layouts.watchOut: Mobile has no room for two columns — needs a total rethink under ~768px.

layouts.name: Kinetic Marquee Bands
layouts.blurb: Giant crossing ribbons of moving type form the actual layout structure.
layouts.rareBecause: Type-as-architecture with motion is loud, hard to keep readable, rarely templated.
layouts.reachFor: Music, streetwear, events, launches — high-energy culture brands.
layouts.watchOut: Motion + huge type = accessibility and readability landmines. Respect reduced-motion.

layouts.name: Parallax Depth Stack
layouts.blurb: Layers move at different speeds to fake real 3D depth on scroll.
layouts.rareBecause: Easy to overdo into nausea; subtle done-right versions are surprisingly rare.
layouts.reachFor: Hero moments, storytelling intros, immersive brand landings.
layouts.watchOut: Heavy on performance and motion-sensitivity. Keep layers few and slow.

layouts.name: Oversized Wordmark Hero
layouts.blurb: The brand name, set enormous, IS the entire first screen.
layouts.rareBecause: Committing a whole viewport to one word terrifies clients who want to 'say more'.
layouts.reachFor: Studios, agencies, personal brands, fashion — confident identity-first sites.
layouts.watchOut: Only works with strong type and a memorable name. Weak wordmark = empty page.

layouts.name: Brutalist / Neubrutalism
layouts.blurb: Raw borders, hard offset shadows, clashing color, zero softness.
layouts.rareBecause: It rejects every 'polished SaaS' convention — reads as ugly-on-purpose.
layouts.reachFor: Dev tools, indie products, Gen-Z brands, anything anti-corporate.
layouts.watchOut: The line between 'intentional brutal' and 'broken' is thin. Commit fully or it looks unfinished.

layouts.name: Newspaper Density (multi-column)
layouts.blurb: Dense narrow text columns with a masthead — print, not web spacing.
layouts.rareBecause: Modern web worships whitespace; deliberate density feels claustrophobic to most.
layouts.reachFor: Editorial, journals, research, long-form culture writing, archives.
layouts.watchOut: Hard to make responsive and scannable. Needs real typographic hierarchy to survive.

layouts.name: Vertical / Rotated Labels
layouts.blurb: Section titles and nav run sideways along the edges.
layouts.rareBecause: Rotated type is hard to read and breaks accessibility if it carries real content.
layouts.reachFor: Fashion, photography, Japanese-influenced minimal, portfolio indexes.
layouts.watchOut: Never put essential nav in rotated-only text. Decorative use only, with upright fallback.

layouts.name: Ransom-Note / Cutout Collage
layouts.blurb: Mixed sizes, fonts, rotations, torn-paper blocks — organized chaos.
layouts.rareBecause: It looks like a mistake to untrained eyes; balance is entirely by feel, not grid.
layouts.reachFor: Zines, music, activism, events, punk/DIY culture brands.
layouts.watchOut: Chaos needs a hidden order. Without a tonal anchor it's just messy.

layouts.name: Infinite Canvas / Spatial
layouts.blurb: A pannable, zoomable 2D space instead of a scrolling page.
layouts.rareBecause: Abandons the page metaphor entirely — most users don't know how to navigate it.
layouts.reachFor: Whiteboard tools, portfolios, mind-map products, spatial brand experiences.
layouts.watchOut: No clear start/end, brutal for SEO and mobile. Give an onboarding + reset-view control.

layouts.name: Terminal / Command-Line UI
layouts.blurb: The site behaves like a console — you type commands to navigate.
layouts.rareBecause: It's the opposite of user-friendly; excludes anyone who won't type.
layouts.reachFor: Dev tools, hacker/security brands, puzzle/ARG experiences, cult-audience products.
layouts.watchOut: Alienates non-technical users completely. Ship a GUI alongside, or gate it as an easter egg.

layouts.name: Radial / Orbital Layout
layouts.blurb: Content orbits a central hub instead of stacking in rows.
layouts.rareBecause: Circular arrangement fights reading order and reflow; almost nothing ships it.
layouts.reachFor: Ecosystem/platform overviews, 'hub' products, planetarium-style brand stories.
layouts.watchOut: Impossible to linearize cleanly for mobile & screen readers. Provide a list fallback.

layouts.name: Command-Palette-First (⌘K)
layouts.blurb: A search/command palette is the primary interface, not a shortcut.
layouts.rareBecause: Making the palette the main path assumes power-users; most designs bury it.
layouts.reachFor: Productivity apps, dev dashboards, internal tools, keyboard-driven audiences.
layouts.watchOut: Discoverability tax for new users. Needs a visible entry point and hints.

layouts.name: Isometric 3D Sections
layouts.blurb: Panels rendered on an isometric plane, stacked in faux-3D.
layouts.rareBecause: Iso projection is a specialist skill; upkeep and responsiveness are painful.
layouts.reachFor: Infra/platform diagrams, game-adjacent brands, technical 'how it works' scenes.
layouts.watchOut: Doesn't reflow — it's essentially a fixed illustration. Heavy to change later.

layouts.name: Cursor Spotlight / Mask Reveal
layouts.blurb: The page is dark until your cursor becomes a moving light that reveals content.
layouts.rareBecause: A masked reveal hides your whole page by default — terrifying for conversion-minded clients.
layouts.reachFor: Portfolios, mystery launches, ARG entries, dramatic brand reveals.
layouts.watchOut: Content hidden behind a cursor is invisible to touch, search, and screen readers. Reveal-all fallback required.

layouts.name: Magnetic Elements
layouts.blurb: Buttons and links bend toward the cursor as it approaches.
layouts.rareBecause: Subtle physics on hover is fiddly to tune and rarely bothered with.
layouts.reachFor: Premium product sites, playful brands, single strong CTA moments.
layouts.watchOut: Overdone it feels slippery and hard to click. Keep pull small; respect reduced-motion.

layouts.name: 3D Tilt Cards
layouts.blurb: Cards pitch and yaw in 3D following the pointer, catching a glare.
layouts.rareBecause: Cheap versions look gimmicky; tasteful depth + light is an actual craft.
layouts.reachFor: Product cards, feature showcases, collectible/NFT-style galleries.
layouts.watchOut: Motion sickness and jank at scale. Limit tilt angle and shadow cost.

layouts.name: Custom-Cursor World
layouts.blurb: The native cursor is replaced by a bespoke object that trails and morphs.
layouts.rareBecause: Hijacking the cursor breaks a sacred OS affordance; most fear the backlash.
layouts.reachFor: Agencies, fashion, experimental portfolios, high-craft brand sites.
layouts.watchOut: Hidden native cursor confuses users and hurts accessibility. Always keep click targets obvious.

layouts.name: Gooey / Metaball Blobs
layouts.blurb: Organic blobs merge and split with the pointer like liquid metal.
layouts.rareBecause: SVG filter goo is obscure and performance-heavy; almost nobody ships it.
layouts.reachFor: Music, beauty, fluid Afro-organic brand worlds, playful landings.
layouts.watchOut: Filters tank performance on low-end devices. Feature-detect and degrade.

layouts.name: Generative Background
layouts.blurb: The backdrop is algorithm-drawn — every visit renders a unique field.
layouts.rareBecause: Non-deterministic visuals scare brand teams who want pixel control.
layouts.reachFor: Generative-art brands, tech, crypto, 'every user is unique' products.
layouts.watchOut: Uncontrolled output can clash with content or contrast. Constrain the palette + seed.

layouts.name: Particle Constellation
layouts.blurb: Points drift and connect with lines that react to the pointer.
layouts.rareBecause: The 'connected dots' hero was trendy, then abandoned — rare done fresh.
layouts.reachFor: Network/AI/data products, community platforms, connection metaphors.
layouts.watchOut: Cliché if generic. Tie particle behavior to your actual brand idea, and cap node count.

layouts.name: Flow-Field / Noise Ribbons
layouts.blurb: Thousands of lines follow an invisible noise field, streaming like wind.
layouts.rareBecause: Requires generative math most teams won't touch; looks like nothing else.
layouts.reachFor: Data-in-motion brands, energy/climate, meditative or scientific products.
layouts.watchOut: Beautiful but heavy and abstract. Ensure text sits on a calm zone.

layouts.name: Per-User Generative Identity
layouts.blurb: The brand pattern/avatar is procedurally generated per visitor or account.
layouts.rareBecause: Tying identity to code output is unusual outside crypto — brand-risky.
layouts.reachFor: Communities, membership products, dev tools, 'your unique X' features.
layouts.watchOut: Some outputs will be ugly. Curate the generative space so every result is on-brand.

layouts.name: Draggable Physics Objects
layouts.blurb: UI elements have weight — you can grab, throw, and collide them.
layouts.rareBecause: Physics on real content fights every layout assumption; almost never shipped.
layouts.reachFor: Playful brands, kids/education, portfolios, interactive press kits.
layouts.watchOut: Users can fling content off-screen. Add gentle bounds + a reset, and a static fallback.
layouts.wireframe: drag me

layouts.name: Gravity Stack / Falling UI
layouts.blurb: Elements drop in and pile up under simulated gravity.
layouts.rareBecause: Physics settling is unpredictable; hard to guarantee a clean final frame.
layouts.reachFor: Launches, playful reveals, 'everything falls into place' storytelling.
layouts.watchOut: Layout isn't pixel-fixed. Only use where the messy pile IS the aesthetic.

layouts.name: Soft-Body / Jelly UI
layouts.blurb: Elements wobble, squash, and stretch like they're made of gel.
layouts.rareBecause: Springy deformation is niche and easy to overdo into nausea.
layouts.reachFor: Toy-like brands, mobile apps, delightful micro-moments.
layouts.watchOut: A little goes far. Reserve for small accents, not whole layouts.

layouts.name: Fluid / Liquid Simulation
layouts.blurb: A real-time fluid backdrop swirls where you move and click.
layouts.rareBecause: WebGL fluid sims are heavy and specialist — genuinely rare in the wild.
layouts.reachFor: Music, art, beauty, immersive hero moments with a 'wow' budget.
layouts.watchOut: GPU-hungry; can drain battery and choke low-end phones. Gate it and fall back to a still.

layouts.name: Audio-Reactive Visuals
layouts.blurb: Bars, shapes, and type pulse in time with sound playing on the page.
layouts.rareBecause: Audio-driven UI needs the Web Audio API + autoplay finesse most avoid.
layouts.reachFor: Music, podcasts, events, launch pages with a signature track.
layouts.watchOut: Autoplay is blocked/annoying; needs a mute-first, opt-in, reduced-motion path.
layouts.wireframe: ♪ live

layouts.name: Time-of-Day Adaptive
layouts.blurb: The whole palette and mood shift with the visitor's local clock.
layouts.rareBecause: Time-linked theming is easy tech but almost nobody bothers to design 3+ states.
layouts.reachFor: Lifestyle, wellness, hospitality, personal brands, journaling apps.
layouts.watchOut: You must design every time-state well, not just invert colors. Test dawn/dusk edges.

layouts.name: Weather / Location-Adaptive
layouts.blurb: The scene mirrors the visitor's real weather — rain, sun, snow overlays.
layouts.rareBecause: Live-data-driven ambiance needs an API + art for each condition; overkill for most.
layouts.reachFor: Travel, outdoor, agriculture, apparel, hyper-local services.
layouts.watchOut: Permission + API dependency; must degrade gracefully when data is missing.
layouts.wireframe: 13°C rain

layouts.name: Scroll-Velocity Reactive
layouts.blurb: How fast you scroll warps the visuals — skew, blur, stretch with speed.
layouts.rareBecause: Velocity-linked distortion is advanced and easy to make queasy.
layouts.reachFor: Editorial, fashion lookbooks, kinetic brand stories.
layouts.watchOut: Fast-scroll blur hurts readability and motion-sensitive users. Cap it, honor reduced-motion.

layouts.name: WebGL 3D Object Hero
layouts.blurb: A real, rotatable 3D model anchors the first screen.
layouts.rareBecause: 3D pipelines (three.js/GLTF) are a specialist skill and a performance tax.
layouts.reachFor: Products with physical form, hardware, footwear, 3D-native brands.
layouts.watchOut: Heavy assets, slow first paint, weak on low-end. Provide a poster-image fallback.
layouts.wireframe: drag to rotate

layouts.name: 3D Configurator
layouts.blurb: Users spin and customize a product live in 3D before buying.
layouts.rareBecause: Full configurators are expensive to build and keep in sync with inventory.
layouts.reachFor: Custom goods, furniture, apparel, vehicles, made-to-order products.
layouts.watchOut: High build + maintenance cost. Only worth it when personalization drives sales.

layouts.name: Z-Depth Fly-Through
layouts.blurb: Scrolling moves the camera forward through layers in space, not down.
layouts.rareBecause: Redefining scroll as z-axis travel is disorienting and hard to build.
layouts.reachFor: Immersive brand films, space/depth metaphors, award-bait showcases.
layouts.watchOut: No scrollbar logic, brutal accessibility & SEO. Needs a linear fallback route.
layouts.wireframe: scroll = forward

layouts.name: 3D Cover-Flow Carousel
layouts.blurb: Items curve back in perspective — the old iPod Cover Flow, reborn.
layouts.rareBecause: Retired years ago as 'dated'; almost nobody revisits it, so it feels fresh again.
layouts.reachFor: Galleries, music/album catalogs, case-study reels, retro-tech brands.
layouts.watchOut: Only shows one item clearly; poor for scanning many options. Pair with a list view.

layouts.name: Curved / Cylindrical Scroll
layouts.blurb: Content sits on a curved surface, bending toward the edges.
layouts.rareBecause: Curving a layout warps type and hit-areas; the math scares people off.
layouts.reachFor: Panoramic galleries, spatial storytelling, 'immersive room' brand pieces.
layouts.watchOut: Edges get unreadable and hard to click. Keep interactive content near center.

layouts.name: Fisheye / Lens Dock
layouts.blurb: Items magnify under a lens as focus passes over them (macOS dock, everywhere).
layouts.rareBecause: Beyond the Mac dock it's almost unused for whole layouts.
layouts.reachFor: Icon menus, tool palettes, playful navigation, creative portfolios.
layouts.watchOut: Magnification shifts neighbors and can mis-target. Keep it to nav, not body content.

layouts.name: Perspective Floor / Horizon
layouts.blurb: Content recedes toward a vanishing point like a road to the horizon.
layouts.rareBecause: True vanishing-point layout is an illustration skill few translate to the web.
layouts.reachFor: Gaming, sci-fi, retro-synth, bold immersive landings.
layouts.watchOut: Distant content is tiny and unusable. It's atmosphere, not a place to put your CTA.

layouts.name: Infinite / Möbius Loop
layouts.blurb: The page has no end — it loops seamlessly back into itself.
layouts.rareBecause: Seamless infinite loops are tricky to build and confuse 'where's the bottom?'.
layouts.reachFor: Manifestos, endless galleries, concept sites, meditative loops.
layouts.watchOut: No footer, no clear end-state, weak for tasks. Give an escape/anchor nav.
layouts.wireframe: ∞

layouts.name: No-Navigation / Explore-Only
layouts.blurb: No menu at all — you discover the site by moving through it.
layouts.rareBecause: Removing nav removes the safety rail everyone relies on; radically hostile.
layouts.reachFor: Art, ARG, exhibitions, cult brand experiences where mystery is the point.
layouts.watchOut: Users get lost and bounce. Only for experiences, never for anything task-driven.
layouts.wireframe: no menu · explore

layouts.name: Invisible / Intent-Reveal UI
layouts.blurb: Controls stay hidden until your behavior signals you need them.
layouts.rareBecause: Betting on intent detection is risky; hidden affordances aren't discoverable.
layouts.reachFor: Reading apps, immersive media, focus/zen tools, premium players.
layouts.watchOut: Undiscoverable by definition. Needs strong hinting and a persistent escape hatch.

layouts.name: Glitch / Datamosh Aesthetic
layouts.blurb: Intentional corruption — RGB split, scanlines, torn pixels.
layouts.rareBecause: It reads as 'broken' to most stakeholders; commitment is everything.
layouts.reachFor: Music, streetwear, cyberpunk, edgy launches, security/hacker brands.
layouts.watchOut: Overuse fatigues fast and can trigger photosensitivity. Use in bursts, offer reduced-motion.

layouts.name: Letter-by-Letter Type Scroll
layouts.blurb: Giant type assembles or animates one glyph at a time as you scroll.
layouts.rareBecause: Per-character scroll choreography is tedious and rarely attempted at scale.
layouts.reachFor: Statements, manifestos, brand intros, typographic showcases.
layouts.watchOut: Slow to read, heavy DOM, weak for content depth. Reserve for a short hero line.

layouts.name: Mission-Control Wall
layouts.blurb: A dense cockpit of live tiles, tickers, and readouts — everything at once.
layouts.rareBecause: Extreme density fights the whitespace orthodoxy; overwhelming if unstructured.
layouts.reachFor: Ops dashboards, trading, logistics, NOC/SOC, power-user analytics.
layouts.watchOut: Cognitive overload without ruthless hierarchy. Earn every tile; group hard.

layouts.name: Node-Graph Home
layouts.blurb: The homepage is an interactive network you traverse node to node.
layouts.rareBecause: Graph-as-navigation is niche, complex, and easy to make unreadable.
layouts.reachFor: Knowledge bases, research, AI/data tools, 'connected thinking' brands.
layouts.watchOut: Hard on mobile, no linear path, SEO-poor. Give a fallback index of the same nodes.

layouts.name: Live Ticker-Driven Layout
layouts.blurb: Streaming real-time data (prices, stats, feeds) sets the page's rhythm.
layouts.rareBecause: Marketing pages almost never wire to live streams; it feels 'alive' and rare.
layouts.reachFor: Fintech, sports, news, marketplaces, anything with real-time proof.
layouts.watchOut: Empty/stale states look broken. Design the no-data and reconnecting states first.

layouts.name: Spreadsheet-as-Interface
layouts.blurb: The product is a living grid of cells — everything editable inline.
layouts.rareBecause: 'It's just a spreadsheet' scares brand teams, but power users love it.
layouts.reachFor: Internal tools, data products, planning apps, ops-heavy audiences.
layouts.watchOut: Intimidating to novices, weak on mobile. Offer guided views over the raw grid.

layouts.name: Playable Hero (mini-game entry)
layouts.blurb: You play a tiny game to enter or unlock the site.
layouts.rareBecause: Gating entry behind play is bold and risks users who just want the content.
layouts.reachFor: Games, agencies, launches, community/ARG experiences.
layouts.watchOut: A wall in front of your content. Always allow 'skip', and keep the game 10-second short.

layouts.name: Character-Select Navigation
layouts.blurb: Choose an avatar/persona and the whole site tailors to that path.
layouts.rareBecause: Front-loading a choice risks friction, and each path multiplies build cost.
layouts.reachFor: Multi-audience brands, personas (great for UJG's Shon/Amazonia/Omegea), education.
layouts.watchOut: N paths = N× the work and QA. Keep personas few and truly distinct.

layouts.name: Quest-Map Progression
layouts.blurb: Content is a map with unlockable stops you progress through.
layouts.rareBecause: Game-map IA is unusual for sites and heavy to design + track state.
layouts.reachFor: Courses, onboarding, community journeys, gamified products.
layouts.watchOut: Progress state adds complexity; linear content trapped in a game shell frustrates. Allow free jump.
layouts.wireframe: start

layouts.name: Inventory-Grid UI
layouts.blurb: Everything lives in a game-style slot grid you equip and arrange.
layouts.rareBecause: Slot-grid IA is unusual outside games; feels novel for a product.
layouts.reachFor: Tools, collections, membership perks, digital-product libraries.
layouts.watchOut: Rigid slots can waste space and confuse. Label slots; don't force the metaphor.

layouts.name: RPG Dialogue-Box Nav
layouts.blurb: You navigate via a game textbox with branching choices.
layouts.rareBecause: Turning navigation into dialogue is slow and radically non-standard.
layouts.reachFor: Story brands, ARGs, persona-led experiences, playful onboarding.
layouts.watchOut: Slow and linear; bad for reference use. Keep it for narrative, add a skip-to-site.

layouts.name: Chaptered Scroll-Film
layouts.blurb: Scrolling plays a scene-by-scene film with pinned, timed beats.
layouts.rareBecause: Scroll-scrubbed video/animation is production-heavy and finicky.
layouts.reachFor: Product launches, mission stories, documentary-style brand pages.
layouts.watchOut: Expensive, heavy, fragile on mobile. Storyboard tightly; keep it under ~6 beats.
layouts.wireframe: SCENE 03

layouts.name: Loading-Screen-as-Content
layouts.blurb: The 'loading' moment is the experience — designed, not skipped.
layouts.rareBecause: Everyone hides loading; making it the show is a rare, delightful inversion.
layouts.reachFor: Games, heavy media sites, launches, brands with personality to spare.
layouts.watchOut: Don't fake slowness. Use only real wait time, and never trap the user in it.

layouts.name: Letterboxed Cinematic Frames
layouts.blurb: Fixed film-ratio frames with black bars — a movie, not a webpage.
layouts.rareBecause: Committing to cinema bars sacrifices space most sites won't give up.
layouts.reachFor: Film, fashion, photography, luxury, trailer-style launches.
layouts.watchOut: Wastes vertical space and fights mobile. Reserve for showcase, not utility pages.
layouts.wireframe: 16:9 FRAME

layouts.name: Cutscene Intro Sequence
layouts.blurb: A short cinematic plays before the site 'begins'.
layouts.rareBecause: Intro sequences risk being the thing everyone clicks 'skip' on.
layouts.reachFor: Games, films, big launches, immersive brand debuts.
layouts.watchOut: Never block returning users; remember 'seen it', always offer skip.
layouts.wireframe: skip ▸

layouts.name: Conversational-First (chat is the site)
layouts.blurb: The primary interface is a conversation, not pages.
layouts.rareBecause: Betting the whole UX on chat is new and abandons familiar navigation.
layouts.reachFor: AI products, support, concierge brands, personal-assistant tools.
layouts.watchOut: Blank-prompt paralysis + no scannable overview. Seed prompts and a visible menu.

layouts.name: Generative UI (assembles from prompt)
layouts.blurb: The interface builds itself around what you ask for, on the fly.
layouts.rareBecause: Runtime-generated layouts are bleeding-edge and hard to make reliable/branded.
layouts.reachFor: AI-native apps, dashboards, tools that adapt per task.
layouts.watchOut: Unpredictable, inconsistent, hard to QA. Constrain to a component whitelist + brand tokens.
layouts.wireframe: ✦ generated

layouts.name: Adaptive / Morphing Layout
layouts.blurb: The layout silently reorganizes around each user's behavior over time.
layouts.rareBecause: Self-rearranging UIs break the 'same place every time' contract users rely on.
layouts.reachFor: Personalized dashboards, media, commerce, returning-user products.
layouts.watchOut: Moving things erodes muscle memory and trust. Adapt slowly, let users pin/lock.

layouts.name: Agentic Canvas (delegate, it builds)
layouts.blurb: You state a goal; an agent assembles the workspace and does the work.
layouts.rareBecause: Delegation-first UX is barely charted — trust, control, and legibility are unsolved.
layouts.reachFor: Next-gen internal tools, automation platforms, power-user AI products.
layouts.watchOut: Opaque automation scares users. Show the plan, keep a human-in-the-loop, make every step reversible.

layouts.name: Growing Vine / Organic UI
layouts.blurb: Navigation and sections grow like vines — branching, unfurling over time.
layouts.rareBecause: Organic growth systems are custom, unpredictable, and rarely built.
layouts.reachFor: Afrofuturist brands (on-mission for UJG), wellness, community, nature.
layouts.watchOut: Growth can tangle and disorient. Constrain the growth grammar; keep paths legible.

layouts.name: Community-Evolving Ecosystem
layouts.blurb: The site visibly changes as the community acts — a living organism.
layouts.rareBecause: State that reflects real collective activity is complex and rarely attempted.
layouts.reachFor: Communities, movements, co-ops, membership brands, live events.
layouts.watchOut: Empty communities look dead. Seed it, and design the low-activity state to still feel alive.
layouts.wireframe: +3 live

layouts.name: Breathing / Ambient Idle
layouts.blurb: When idle, the whole page softly breathes — a slow, living pulse.
layouts.rareBecause: Ambient idle life is subtle work most skip; it makes a page feel alive.
layouts.reachFor: Wellness, meditation, brand homes, ambient/idle screens.
layouts.watchOut: Motion for motion's sake distracts. Keep it barely-there; pause on interaction + reduced-motion.

layouts.name: Bio-Responsive Growth
layouts.blurb: Visuals mimic organic growth/decay tied to real usage or time.
layouts.rareBecause: Simulating biological systems in UI is deeply niche and hard to control.
layouts.reachFor: Sustainability, health, generative-brand, long-term membership products.
layouts.watchOut: Abstract and slow to read. Anchor it to a clear metric so growth means something.
